what_this_is: A machine-readable definition of a protein-production chassis that does NOT exist in any laboratory. It is the designed organism, written down so it can be queried. Base organism is extant; the engineered modules are proposals carrying published precedent, not validated constructs.

base_organism.headroom_evidence: These proteins can be expressed at levels exceeding 40% of total protein while maintaining yeast growth
base_organism.selection_caveat: Yeast is also the obvious choice. The four architectural rules are tested by what they reject (all prokaryotes, JCVI-syn3.0), not by what they select.

global_constraints.statement: Total heterologous protein must stay under 40% of cell protein
global_constraints.evidence: exceeding 40% of total protein while maintaining yeast growth

global_constraints.statement: No single protein above 15% of cell protein
global_constraints.evidence: The limits of some glycolytic proteins were up to 15% of the total cellular protein

global_constraints.statement: Independent switches simultaneously active should stay at or below about 12
global_constraints.status: measured for CRISPRi in E. coli; assumed transferable
global_constraints.evidence: CRISPRi cannot support more than about a dozen simultaneous gRNAs before the fold repression of any individual gRNA drops below 10x
global_constraints.caveat: Not binding at 5 engineered switches. Retained because the count may grow.

global_constraints.statement: Disulfide formation requires an oxidising compartment; cytoplasm is reducing
global_constraints.evidence: Both eukaryotic and prokaryotic organisms keep their cytoplasm reduced
global_constraints.resolution: Route disulfide-bearing products through the ER and secretory pathway. Native in all eukaryotes; no organelle engineering required.

capabilities.name: Codon usage compatible with host tRNA pool
Folding and chaperone capacity
capabilities.note: ER chaperone machinery; overexpression of Kar2p, PDI, Ero1 studied

capabilities.name: Disulfide bond formation
capabilities.note: Native PDI/Ero1 in the ER; requires secretory routing

capabilities.name: O-glycosylation
capabilities.note: O-mannosylation present; differs from human O-GalNAc

capabilities.name: Other PTMs (phosphorylation, lipidation, processing)
capabilities.note: Many present, some absent; not enumerated

capabilities.name: Stress response capacity
capabilities.note: Tolerance is the least assessed category in this project

capabilities.name: Culture-condition range (O2, temperature, salt)
capabilities.note: Facultative: aerobic and anaerobic metabolism both available

engineered_modules.goal: Replace high-mannose yeast N-glycans with human-like structures
engineered_modules.published_precedent: Glycan humanisation has been achieved in yeast; pcSecYeastSpecies includes humanized glycosylation modules
engineered_modules.cost_status: not measured anywhere; this is the most expensive module and its cost is unknown
engineered_modules.unverified: Part list assembled from the general glycoengineering literature, not from one validated published strain.

engineered_modules.goal: Supply UDP-GlcNAc and UDP-galactose at the rate humanised glycans consume them
engineered_modules.published_precedent: Sugar-nucleotide supply is a named bottleneck in glycoengineering
engineered_modules.coupling: Only required when MOD-glycan is active. Costs must be summed with it, not counted separately.

engineered_modules.goal: Raise secretory flux above native capacity
engineered_modules.published_precedent: Overexpression of secretion helpers PDI1, ERO1, SSO2, KAR2/BiP and HAC1; pcSecYeast identified overexpression targets for improved recombinant protein production
engineered_modules.unverified: Which helpers to overexpress is protein-specific. Structural Homology Fails to Predict Secretion Efficiency in Pichia pastoris reports architecturally similar proteins diverging under identical engineering.

engineered_modules.goal: Express coding sequences beyond routine size without truncation or recombination
engineered_modules.published_precedent: A 106 kb biosynthetic cluster has been assembled and expressed heterologously
engineered_modules.unverified: The cited precedent is a multi-gene cluster, not a single large protein. Relevance is assumed, not shown.

engineered_modules.goal: Keep heterologous expression inside the proteome budget by switching modules rather than running them constitutively
engineered_modules.published_precedent: Proteome allocation constraints are modelled in pcSecYeast and pcSecYeastSpecies
parts_required: a small set of orthogonal regulators (5 addresses is within routine reach)
engineered_modules.note: Demoted from architectural requirement to optimisation when scope narrowed to proteins. See protocol/scope-proteins-v1.md.

known_weaknesses_of_base_organism: Crabtree effect: ferments to ethanol even with oxygen present, wasting carbon
Native N-glycans are high-mannose and need engineering for therapeutic products
Not the best secretor; Komagataella phaffii is better, and pcSecYeastSpecies now models it
what_this_object_cannot_do: It cannot predict titre. No quantitative model is attached in version 1.
It carries no measured proteome cost for any engineered module, so global_constraints cannot yet be checked against a resolved configuration.
Every module is a proposal with published precedent, not a validated construct. Nothing here has been built.
Confidence values are the author's judgement from abstracts and README files, not calibrated estimates.
Tolerance (F3, F4) is the least assessed area and the literature calls it the usual binding constraint.

external_models: github.com/LiLabTsinghua/pcSecYeastSpecies (updated 2025-12, MATLAB, covers S. cerevisiae, K. phaffii, K. marxianus)
